expected_approaches.summary: Maintain a window and the last position of each character.
common_failure_modes: moving left backward for a stale last-seen index

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int lengthOfLongestSubstring(string s) { unordered_map<char,int> last; int left=0, answer=0; for(int right=0; right<(int)s.size(); ++right) { if(last.count(s[right])) left=max(left,last[s[right]]+1); last[s[right]]=right; answer=max(answer,right-left+1); } return answer; } };

class Solution { public int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) { java.util.Map<Character,Integer> last=new java.util.HashMap<>(); int left=0, answer=0; for(int right=0; right<s.length(); right++){ if(last.containsKey(s.charAt(right))) left=Math.max(left,last.get(s.charAt(right))+1); last.put(s.charAt(right),right); answer=Math.max(answer,right-left+1); } return answer; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: The left boundary never moves backward.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Distinguish expected from guaranteed lookup complexity.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Discuss storage for a larger alphabet.

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test whether the candidate can defend a monotonic left boundary.
sample_phrasings: What prevents your left boundary from moving backward?

level_considerations.guidance: Prefer invariant explanation over implementation trivia.

reference_reasoning: The pack supplies reviewed priors; it is not a whitelist of valid candidate approaches.
